name: DIY pattern — Kafka + Flink/Spark + Valkey/Redis stitched
category: Horizontal infra-platform competitors — the 'do it yourself' baseline that most fraud / ad-tech / behavioral-analytics teams currently maintain in-house
parent_research_topic: Beava's current market position — competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: This 'archetype' is not a single vendor — it is the engineering pattern most fraud / ad-tech / behavioral-analytics teams maintain in-house in 2025-2026, made out of three composable layers: (i) an event bus (Apache Kafka 4.0 KRaft-only after March 2025, Redpanda, AWS MSK / Kinesis, Confluent Cloud, WarpStream-now-Confluent-BYOC, AutoMQ, Aiven for Kafka, Azure Event Hubs, GCP Pub/Sub); (ii) a stateful stream processor (Apache Flink — the dominant choice with named production users at Alibaba 40B events/day, DoorDash 100Bs of events/day, Uber, Lyft, Stripe, Netflix, LinkedIn, BMW, Apple; Apache Spark Structured Streaming with Real-Time Mode GA on Databricks Runtime 16.4+; Kafka Streams for JVM-embedded teams; ksqlDB feature-frozen at Confluent after Immerok acquisition pivoted them to Flink SQL); and (iii) a low-latency online store (Redis OSS / Redis 8 tri-licensed AGPLv3+RSALv2+SSPLv1 since May 2025, Valkey BSD-3-clause LF-stewarded — default for AWS ElastiCache and GCP Memorystore, Dragonfly BSL multi-threaded, Aerospike commercial flash+RAM hybrid, AWS DynamoDB, RocksDB, Cassandra). The vast majority of named real-time-fraud / personalization / metering production architectures cited in 2024-2025 industry blogs (DoorDash Riviera, Airwallex feature store on Flink, Wix on Flink, Grab GrabDefence on Kafka+Flink, Whatnot pre-Chalk, Stripe Radar internals, the AWS RTB Fabric reference architecture) follow the same Kafka + Flink + (Redis | Aerospike | ElastiCache) shape, often with an offline feature-store layer (Feast / Tecton / Hopsworks / Chalk / Fennel) bolted on top for training-serving parity. Per Datadog's 2024-2025 telemetry survey: 63% of Redis users run it as part of a larger stack, 45% alongside Kafka, 31% alongside Flink — confirming the DIY archetype's dominance. Beava replaces this entire three-layer stack with a single Rust binary; it competes against the pattern, not against any individual product within it.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: By use case: (1a CNP fraud) Kafka + Flink as the auth-time scoring pipeline at issuers/PSPs, Redis or Aerospike for the velocity-counter hot tier, Lua scripts or Flink CEP for the threshold rules — Stripe Radar's documented 1-2 ms inference + ~98 ms feature collection is the published version of this; large PSPs / acquirers (Worldpay, Adyen, Stripe non-Radar) are publicly on this stack. (1b instant-payments fraud) Same triad inside banks / PSPs for FedNow ($10M limit Nov 2025), RTP, SEPA Instant (Oct 2025 mandate), UPI — Kafka as the pacs.008 message bus, Flink as the velocity / mule-detection aggregator, Redis as the inline credit-balance / sanctions-cache lookup; Feedzai (~$8B/yr processed), Featurespace ARIC at HSBC/NatWest/Worldpay, NICE Actimize, ACI ReD, Hawk.AI all run variants. (2 account abuse / bot defence) Kafka or direct WAF push, Flink or Kafka Streams for rolling failure-ratio / n_unique computation, Redis-Lua for the inline auth-gate counter (the Auth0 / Castle / Cloudflare BM pattern is the textbook version, ~26B credential-stuffing attempts/month industry-wide) — Cloudflare runs an in-house Rust + RocksDB + Durable Objects variant. (6 recsys / ranking) Kafka clickstream, Flink/Spark for in-session rolling popularity and per-(user, category) affinity, Redis / Aerospike / DynamoDB for the online feature serving at 100-500 candidate fan-out — DoorDash Riviera (Flink-based, declarative-YAML, reduced feature dev time from weeks to hours and feature-engineering codebase by 70%); Airwallex (Flink + Redis + Kafka dual-sink) is the public reference; Whatnot ran a DIY Flink+Redis variant before migrating to Chalk; Pinterest Manas, Instacart Griffin, Meesho, Sony PlayStation on Aerospike are all variants. (14b usage-based billing / metering) Kafka raw-event log + Flink or custom Go consumer + ClickHouse aggregator + Redis-Lua for the inline quota gate (Lago's 1M EPS public reference on ClickHouse Cloud, OpenMeter's YC-backed Kafka+ClickHouse+CloudEvents architecture, Stripe Meter Event Streams v2 capped at 10k req/s livemode, Orb 250k+ EPS SQL-over-raw-events) — followed by an external rating / invoicing layer (Stripe Billing, Metronome-acquired-by-Stripe-Jan-2026 at ~$1B, Orb, Chargebee, Zuora). Funding/M&A status of the DIY layer's commercial backers in 2025-2026: Confluent (NASDAQ:CFLT, acquired WarpStream Sep 2024 and Immerok 2023), Redis Inc. (private; relicensed to SSPL/RSALv2 Mar 2024 then tri-licensed AGPLv3 May 2025; acquired Decodable Sep 2025 and Featureform Oct 2025), Databricks (acquired Tecton 2025 and Fennel Apr 2025), Aerospike (private commercial); Materialize (~$108M Series C 2021, visible 2024-2025 layoff signal); RisingWave (~$46M Series A); the Apache-2.0 Rust single-binary entrants (Arroyo, Bytewax, Pathway, Fluvio, EventFlux, RisingWave) are seed-to-Series-A scale and are the structural cousins of beava on the streaming-engine layer. [uncertain] exact per-team headcount and dollar-cost numbers for each DIY deployment are private; Datadog 2024-2025 telemetry, Confluent's 2025 Data Streaming Report (4,000 IT leaders, 86% say data streaming is a top strategic investment), and the Confluent 'self-managed Kafka has 3-5x higher TCO than Confluent Cloud' line are the public proxies.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Mixed across the three layers, and in 2025-2026 the answer 'no single Apache-2.0 path through the DIY stack survives' is the unique-to-beava wedge. Layer-by-layer: (event bus) Apache Kafka itself is Apache-2.0 — fine; managed Confluent products are commercial; Redpanda Community Edition is BSL, Enterprise commercial; AutoMQ is Apache-2.0; WarpStream is now Confluent commercial BYOC; AWS MSK / Azure Event Hubs / GCP Pub/Sub are proprietary managed services. (stream processor) Flink, Spark, Kafka Streams are Apache-2.0; ksqlDB is Confluent Community License (source-available, not OSI-OSS); Materialize is BSL 1.1 with a Community Edition capped at 24 GiB RAM / 48 GiB disk; RisingWave is Apache-2.0; Confluent Cloud Flink / AWS MSF / Databricks Real-Time Mode are managed-only. (online store) Redis 8 is tri-licensed AGPLv3 + RSALv2 + SSPLv1 since May 2025 — the AGPLv3 option is OSI but its copyleft scope blocks many enterprise procurement filters, and the 2024 SSPL/RSALv2 'rug-pull' burned community trust; Valkey is BSD-3-clause (the cloud default — AWS ElastiCache for Valkey, GCP Memorystore for Valkey, Ubuntu 26.04 ships Valkey as the `redis` package; 83% large-enterprise adoption per Percona's 2025 survey); Dragonfly is BSL; Aerospike Enterprise is commercial (with an AGPL Community Edition); RonDB is GPLv2; KeyDB is BSD-3 under Snap. Net: a buyer can today stitch an entirely permissive DIY stack — Apache Kafka + Apache Flink + Valkey BSD-3 — IF they accept the operational burden, and that combination is increasingly the default for new builds in 2025-2026. Beava's Apache-2.0 single-binary posture is no longer uniquely-different on license vs Valkey, but it remains strictly more permissive than Redis 8 / Dragonfly / Materialize / Aerospike / Tecton-managed / Chalk-managed / Redis Feature Form, and it collapses the three-layer license-policy review into one.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: High. The DIY stack is precisely the architecture that hyperscalers are now bundling into one SKU and pitching as 'good enough' replacements: Confluent Cloud for Apache Flink unifies Kafka + Flink + Schema Registry + Connect in one offering and explicitly markets a '60% lower TCO than self-managed Kafka' / '40% lower TCO than self-managed Kafka via Confluent Platform' / '3-5x TCO multiplier on self-managed at scale' positioning (2025 Data Streaming Report, 4,000 IT leaders surveyed); AWS bundles MSK + Managed Service for Apache Flink + ElastiCache for Valkey (the default ElastiCache engine, 20% cheaper than Redis SKU); Databricks Real-Time Mode (GA Aug 2025, Databricks Runtime 16.4+) lands Flink-equivalent sub-300 ms p99 latency inside the same Spark runtime customers already pay for, plus Tecton (acquired 2025) and Fennel (acquired Apr 2025) folded into the Lakebase/Feature Serving offering; Redis Feature Form (Redis-acquired-Featureform Oct 2025, preview Apr 2026) folds Featureform's batch+stream + multi-tenancy + RBAC into Redis Cloud; Snowflake Snowpipe Streaming + Dynamic Tables and Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Intelligence are the same play from adjacent hyperscalers. The hyperscaler bundle's wedge against beava is precisely the buyer who already pays for one of these clouds and would rather absorb a managed-Flink + managed-Valkey SKU than introduce a new single-binary OSS process. Beava's counter-wedge is the buyer who wants to ESCAPE the bundle — either for ops simplicity (one binary, no JobManager + TaskManagers + Schema Registry + connector library + state backend + checkpoint sink to operate) or for license discipline (no AGPLv3-Redis / no BSL-Materialize / no managed-only-RTM) or for raw latency (sub-ms TCP+msgpack vs Redis-Lua 1-5 ms, which Flink + Redis-Lua-on-ElastiCache cannot collapse). For mid-market accounts not yet locked into a hyperscaler, this wedge is real; for enterprise accounts already on the bundle, beava is an uphill displacement story.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: The DIY pattern is, by definition, the Kafka-shaped integration surface incarnate. Producers are Kafka topics consumed by Flink/Spark (FLIP-27 source API, hundreds of Flink CDC connectors via Debezium for Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB, Kafka Connect for everything else); intermediate state is Flink's RocksDB state backend with checkpointing to S3 / HDFS / GCS; downstream sinks are Kafka topics, JDBC, Iceberg / Delta Lake, Cassandra, S3 Parquet, and the online store (Redis / Valkey / DynamoDB / Aerospike) fronted by application code that calls GET / batch_get. SDK-direct-push patterns (mobile SDK → Kafka via HTTPS, Segment/RudderStack/Snowplow/PostHog/Mixpanel collectors writing to Kafka) are common producers but always terminate at a Kafka topic before the streaming engine sees them. The IoT cohort uses AWS IoT Rules / Azure IoT Hub egress / MQTT brokers fronting Kafka. The metering cohort (Lago, OpenMeter, Stripe Meter Event Streams v2) accepts direct HTTP CloudEvents and then often shoves them into Kafka or Pulsar for the durability layer. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 + framed TCP+msgpack :8081 push surface is fundamentally NOT this shape — it expects the producer to push events directly to beava and the consumer to pull features from beava, never moving through a broker. This is a fit for application-direct-push and webhook-driven flows (Stripe charge webhooks, mobile-SDK fraud-signal push, the metering-collector pattern, the WAF / auth-gate event-emit pattern) and an active friction for any buyer who has already standardized on Kafka and whose entire org's event-of-record is a Kafka topic (which is the DoorDash / Uber / Lyft / Rivian / Volkswagen / large-PSP / Confluent-customer archetype). Adding a Kafka consumer bridge is a few-hundred-line job and the single most-frequently-cited gap from the H1-H4 use-case research — its absence in v0 is the primary adoption friction for buyers already inside this DIY archetype.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, by definition. The DIY stack feeds both: (a) a rules engine — Flink CEP for in-engine pattern matching, Drools / OPA / FEEL for application-side, Redis-Lua scripts for inline counter thresholds, Confluent ksqlDB / Snowflake / Materialize SQL recording rules for the SQL-on-streams cohort; and (b) one or more ML scorers — XGBoost / LightGBM (the production fraud / recsys baseline), increasingly TabTransformer / two-tower retrieval / cross-encoder rerankers / DLRM (Whatnot, Pinterest, Meta), ONNX served from a Python or Triton process pulling features via batch_get from the online store. The DIY stack treats the streaming engine as the feature-pipeline factory and the online store as the substrate; the scoring engine sits one process boundary away and reads features at decision time. Beava matches this exact seam — it serves features to whichever scoring engine the buyer runs, without trying to be the scoring engine itself — which is why beava can credibly slot underneath the same scorers (Feedzai, Featurespace, NICE Actimize, in-house XGBoost) that the DIY stack feeds today, IF the buyer is willing to accept a different ingest model (push-on-event instead of Kafka-consume).

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Beava's wedge against the DIY pattern is operational simplicity, not raw perf. Concretely: (1) One binary vs three+ moving systems — a baseline Flink job demands a JobManager + TaskManagers + state backend (RocksDB) + checkpoint sink (S3/HDFS) + a Kafka cluster (3+ brokers + KRaft controllers post-Kafka-4.0) + a Redis/Valkey/Aerospike instance + a feature-store layer (Feast/Tecton/Hopsworks/Chalk/Fennel) for offline-online parity — typically a 5-12-engineer platform team to operate continuously per Confluent's 2025 cost-of-ownership writeups and the public 'self-managed Kafka 3-5x higher TCO than Confluent Cloud' line; beava is one Rust process with WAL + snapshot, started by a single `./beava` command. The 'fragmentation' pain (Lua + SQL + Flink-DSL + Java DataStream API + Python feature definitions, each with different deploy and observability surfaces) is collapsed into the Python @bv.event / @bv.table SDK plus a wire-JSON expression grammar. (2) No Kafka cluster cost and no inter-AZ replication tax — Kafka's hidden inter-AZ networking is publicly cited as the single largest hidden Kafka cost (AWS $0.01/GB each direction = $0.02/GB effective; a typical workload with 100 MB/s sustained writes and 3-broker replication can bill $30k-$100k+/year on cross-AZ alone before any compute, per AutoMQ and Confluent infrastructure-cost writeups); WarpStream / AutoMQ / Aiven Diskless / Confluent PNI all exist explicitly to fix this, and the existence of those products is the public proof that the problem is real. Beava has no broker, no replication, no inter-AZ cost. (3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get vs Redis-Lua 1-5 ms vs Vertex AI FS ~30 ms vs Tecton-published 0.8 ms — beava sits in Aerospike / Dragonfly latency territory on commodity hardware with the published 684k EPS sustained on a single Apple-M4 core as the headline. The Redis-Lua-script-as-bottleneck pain (the 'API response went from 150 ms to 3 s overnight because the Lua optimizer became a bottleneck' shape) is documented community pain in 2024-2025; beava's declarative @bv.table primitives avoid this class of bug entirely. (4) ~50-60 declarative aggregation primitives (count, sum, mean, var, std, n_unique with HLL, quantile with t-digest, CMS top-k, exponential decay, recency, velocity, distance, last-N lists) baked into the server — the DIY stack hand-rolls each of these in Flink Java / Flink SQL / Lua scripts / RedisTimeSeries downsampling, each with its own correctness + drift + on-call surface. The DoorDash Riviera precedent (declarative YAML over Flink, dev time reduced from weeks to hours, feature-engineering codebase reduced by 70%) is the public proof that declarative beats hand-rolled — except DoorDash still has to run Flink underneath; beava removes that floor. (5) No single Apache-2.0 path post-Redis-BSL fully exists across the DIY stack — Valkey (BSD-3) + Apache Kafka (Apache-2.0) + Apache Flink (Apache-2.0) is the closest, but the moment a buyer needs probabilistic structures (Bloom/CMS/top-K/t-digest), they reach for Redis modules which are now under the Redis 8 tri-license (AGPLv3 carries copyleft procurement risk; RSALv2/SSPLv1 are not OSI). Beava's Apache-2.0 single-binary collapses the three-layer license-policy review into one and is a real wedge for license-disciplined buyers (regulated finance, regtech, vendor-embed cases). (6) WAL+snapshot per-entity durability with refuse-on-network-FS invariant — closer in semantics to Aerospike's per-key persistence than to Redis AOF's per-instance flush, without the Aerospike Enterprise license. (7) Apache-2.0 with no open-core split, no SSPL/BSL trap, no Enterprise Edition that emerges 18 months in — strictly more permissive than every commercial competitor in the DIY assembly except Valkey (comparable).
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: The DIY stack does many things beava cannot — those are the credible objections from buyers who already run it. In rough priority order: (1) No Kafka / Kinesis / Pulsar consumer in v0 — every published DIY-stack reference (DoorDash, Uber, Lyft, Stripe, Airwallex, Wix, Grab, Whatnot pre-Chalk, the AWS RTB Fabric reference architecture) assumes the event-of-record is a Kafka topic; beava's push-only ingress forces re-plumbing the producers or running a sidecar consumer. This is the single most-cited adoption friction. (2) No general stream processing — beava does NOT do windowed joins, Flink CEP / complex event patterns, cross-stream enrichment via Flink's DataStream API, or arbitrary SQL transforms; the buyer who actually needs Flink-class capability cannot replace Flink with beava, only the count/mean/quantile/decay slice that runs on top of it. (3) No exactly-once semantics — Flink's checkpointing + 2PC sinks, Spark Structured Streaming's idempotent micro-batch + Delta, RisingWave's barrier checkpoints all give exactly-once; beava is at-least-once at best. This is a hard disqualifier for billing-grade metering (use 14b) and PSD2 TRA / chargeback-liability counters (use 1a). (4) No event-time processing in v0 — beava is processing-time-only and rejects `event_time` / `event_time_ms` fields explicitly (`unknown_field_event_time_v0`); Flink/Spark/Materialize/RisingWave all handle event-time + watermarks natively. Disqualifying for IoT telemetry with intermittent connectivity, mobile SDK buffered uploads, replay from Kafka archive, instant-payments fraud where pacs.008 timestamps lag arrival. (5) No TLS / no auth / no RBAC — disqualifying anywhere events cross trust boundaries; every named DIY-stack alternative (managed Confluent, MSK, MSF, ElastiCache, Aerospike, Tecton, Hopsworks, Chalk, Feast-on-Redis) ships TLS + IAM out of the box. (6) No in-process sharding / no horizontal scale — single beava node caps around 684k EPS / tens of GB hot state; the DIY stack with Flink + Kafka + Redis-Cluster routinely scales horizontally to millions of EPS (DoorDash 100Bs of events/day, Pinterest Manas 1.2M user-actions/sec, Whatnot on Chalk 300M features/sec). (7) No cross-region active-active replication — fraud counters, credit-balance wallets, frequency caps for global tenants need consistent counters across regions; the DIY stack uses Kafka MirrorMaker 2 / Cluster Linking + Aerospike XDR / Redis Active-Active geo-replication. (8) No idempotency-key dedup primitive on the wire — every billing-metering, ad-tech-cap-counter and exact fraud-counter use case requires increment-once-per-event-id-within-window (Stripe pattern: 24h dedup, OpenMeter pattern: 32d); the DIY stack assembles this via Kafka transactional writes + idempotent Flink sinks + Redis SETNX, all explicit. (9) No durable raw-event log as a first-class artifact — the DIY stack's Kafka topic IS the raw-event log, with multi-year retention (or S3 archive via Tiered Storage / Iceberg); beava's WAL+snapshot survives restarts but cannot satisfy 'reconstruct December's invoice in March from the durable raw event log' (use 14b), which is table-stakes SOX/SOC1. (10) No SQL surface — Flink SQL, Spark SQL, ksqlDB, Materialize, RisingWave all expose CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW for analysts; beava is Python-SDK-only. (11) No triggers / 'fire when counter crosses threshold' — the DIY stack pairs Flink with downstream Kafka topics + alerting workers; beava forces the caller to poll. (12) No native vector / ANN — Redis 8 ships Vector Sets (HNSW beta), Aerospike Vector Search; beava is feature-serving only. (13) No managed/hosted offering — every DIY-stack alternative has a managed tier (Confluent Cloud, AWS MSK + MSF + ElastiCache, GCP Memorystore for Valkey, Aiven, Databricks RTM, Tecton, Hopsworks, Chalk, Fennel-on-Databricks, Redis Feature Form); beava buyers must operate the box themselves. (14) No 1+ tier-1 public reference customer in this segment — every DIY-stack incumbent has at least one (DoorDash, Uber, Stripe, Whatnot, PayPal, Criteo, JPMorgan, Pinterest); beava has none.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 6-12mo. The gating items for beava to be a credible 'collapsed DIY stack' for a mid-market buyer (not tier-1 scale): (a) a Kafka/Kinesis/MQTT consumer bridge sidecar so the buyer doesn't have to re-plumb their producers — a few-hundred-line job individually but the single most-cited gap across the use-case research; (b) TLS + auth (mTLS + bearer-token + RBAC) so it can cross trust boundaries — a couple weeks of work, table-stakes; (c) event-time + watermarking so late-arriving events don't break IoT and CDC use cases — a multi-week design + implementation job that touches the wire format, but feasible without breaking v0's processing-time-only invariant if implemented as a v1 opt-in; (d) idempotency-key dedup primitive on the ingest path matching the Stripe 24h / OpenMeter 32d patterns — a couple weeks; (e) some form of horizontal sharding-by-key-prefix or replication for the >684k EPS / >50 GB hot-state tenants — the biggest architectural lift, plausibly the 'beyond 12mo' work for tier-1 scale but a documented sidecar shard router could cover mid-market in 1-2 months; (f) at-least-once-with-idempotency-key Kafka-consumer semantics + a Kafka producer sink for the trigger / downstream-event-emit path — a few weeks. None individually is a multi-quarter job, but together they are the 6-12 month roadmap before beava is credible against a buyer comparing it against (Kafka + Flink + Redis) for a production fraud / recsys / metering deployment. Tier-1-scale (DoorDash / Stripe / Pinterest / global PSP / global card network) wins are 12mo+ even with all of the above shipped, because they additionally require multi-region active-active and managed-tier offerings that beava does not have any structural progress on as of v0.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: No public beava users running on the 'replace the DIY stack' positioning. The use-case-level deep-dives (1a, 1b, 2, 6, 14b) all explicitly flag 'no public users of beava on this use case yet'. Repo evidence: ~60 aggregation primitives in `python/beava/_agg.py` covering the count / sum / mean / var / std / n_unique / quantile (t-digest) / HLL / CMS / exponential-decay / recency / velocity / distance surface that DIY-stack users today hand-roll in Flink Java + Redis Lua; runnable demos exist in `python/beava/demos/{adtech, ecommerce, fraud}` with the fraud demo (`schema.json` + `events.jsonl` keyed on card_hash) and ecommerce demo (`PageView` / `AddToCart` / `Purchase` keyed on user_id / sku) being exactly the DIY-stack-replacement shapes for use 1a (CNP fraud) and use 6 (recsys). `crates/beava-bench/src/workloads/fraud.rs` plus `crates/beava-bench/configs/fraud-team.json` plus the `fraud_team_validates_against_agg_op_descriptor.rs` test show 'fraud team' is a tracked benchmark workload. No purpose-built demos for instant-payments fraud (1b), bot-defence / credential-stuffing (2), or usage-based-billing / metering (14b) ship as of the snapshot — these would be high-leverage adds to make the wedge concrete. Comparable adoption signals at DIY-stack incumbents (validating the segment shape, not beava): DoorDash Riviera reduced feature dev time from weeks to hours and feature-engineering codebase by 70% by moving from hand-rolled Flink to declarative YAML over Flink (the public proof that declarative beats imperative even before single-binary); Airwallex documented dual-sink Redis+Kafka feature store on Flink as a multi-engineer multi-quarter build; Confluent's 2025 Data Streaming Report (4,000 IT leaders) cites 86% strategic-investment, 44% reporting 5x+ ROI, and 'self-managed Kafka 3-5x higher TCO than autoscaling managed services'; the AutoMQ + WarpStream-now-Confluent + Aiven Diskless cohort exist explicitly to fix the Kafka inter-AZ networking cost (cited as the single largest hidden Kafka infrastructure cost). The 'Kafka is dead, long live Kafka' WarpStream launch in August 2023 — followed by Confluent's $200M+ acquisition of WarpStream in September 2024 — is the canonical industry meme that the DIY-stack's cost / complexity profile is a real and bookable market opportunity. Redis 8's May 2025 tri-license including AGPLv3 + the September 2025 Redis-Decodable acquisition + the October 2025 Redis-Featureform acquisition + the April 2026 Redis Feature Form preview launch are the public proof that the same dynamic is now playing out at the online-store layer. Net: the DIY stack is an enormous, well-funded, and increasingly-bundled-by-hyperscalers market with documented operational pain; the segment is winnable for a single-binary OSS challenger only in the narrow seam where (a) the buyer is mid-market (sub-tier-1 scale), (b) the buyer values ops simplicity over feature breadth, (c) the buyer has license discipline that rules out Redis 8 / Materialize / managed-only options, and (d) the buyer's producer is HTTP/SDK-direct-push rather than Kafka-shaped. That seam exists and is large enough to support a credible OSS product; tier-1 wins are not realistic in the next 12 months.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Lead — this is beava's foundational wedge and the only narrative where Apache-2.0 + single binary + ~60 declarative primitives + sub-ms TCP genuinely collapses three layers of moving systems into one. Pitch beava as 'the Kafka + Flink + Redis replacement for the mid-market team that doesn't have a 5-person platform team to operate the DIY stack' — not as a 'Flink replacement' or a 'Redis replacement' individually (each of those framings invites a use-case where beava loses on day one, per H2 Watch and H3 Compete). The wedge is strongest at fraud / fraud-adjacent buyers (use 1a, 1b, 2) who are not Stripe-scale, at mid-market recsys / personalization shops (use 6) below Whatnot-on-Chalk scale, and at AI-platform / API-as-a-product metering buyers (use 14b) who need the inline-quota-gate slice but not the full SOX-grade invoicing replacement. Avoid head-on framing battles against Confluent Cloud Flink / Databricks RTM / Tecton-on-Databricks bundles at tier-1 accounts — beava loses those on day one until horizontal scaling + managed-tier + exactly-once + Kafka-consumer ship. Use the 6-12 month roadmap (Kafka consumer + TLS/auth + idempotency-key + event-time + sharding) to convert Lead from 'demo' to 'productized'. The DIY-stack archetype's documented operational pain (Kafka inter-AZ cost, Redis-Lua bottlenecks, Flink expert teams of 5-12, Redis BSL/AGPL license uncertainty) is beava's single largest in-market tailwind for 2025-2026.
